submissions.title: Dacryocystorhinostomy (DCR): Surgical Masterclass, Pearls & Pitfalls
submissions.summary: An authoritative, textbook-grade surgical guide detailing surgical anatomy, external vs. endoscopic DCR techniques, step-by-step algorithms, high-yield surgical tricks, and strategies to prevent and manage critical complications.

submissions.title: Mastering PDR Regression: Clinical Markers & Post-Treatment Assessment
submissions.summary: This guide delineates the objective clinical signs of proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) regression following pan-retinal photocoagulation (PRP) or anti-VEGF therapy. Recognizing these markers is vital for preventing sight-threatening complications.

submissions.title: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) in Diabetic Retinopathy & Retinal Detachment: A Comprehensive Guide
submissions.summary: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) is a cornerstone surgical procedure for managing complex vitreoretinal diseases, particularly sight-threatening complications of diabetic retinopathy and various forms of retinal detachment. This infographic explores the indications, principles, techniques, and considerations for PPV, providing a detailed, resident-level overview of this vital ophthalmic intervention.

submissions.title: Clinical Mastery: Resolving CRVO vs. Diabetic Retinopathy
submissions.summary: A high-yield comparative analysis between a resolving Central Retinal Vein Occlusion (CRVO) and Diabetic Retinopathy (DR). Distinguishing these entities is critical for management, as CRVO requires ruling out underlying systemic vascular risk, while DR mandates glycemic control and metabolic optimization.

submissions.title: The Silent Aftermath: Regressed PDR & Chronic Retinal Vein Occlusion
submissions.summary: A comprehensive guide to identifying the 'burned-out' or regressed signs of Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR) and the sequelae of old Central (CRVO) or Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion (BRVO). Essential for differentiating benign collaterals from active neovascularization.

submissions.title: Ischemic Maculopathy in Diabetic Retinopathy
submissions.summary: A devastating complication of diabetic retinopathy characterized by the loss of the foveal capillary network. Diagnosis relies on identifying foveal avascular zone (FAZ) enlargement and irregularity, often leading to irreversible central vision loss despite management of macular edema.

submissions.title: VIP:::FRCS:DKA: Systemic Emergency & Ophthalmic Implications
submissions.summary: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) is a life-threatening triad of hyperglycemia, ketosis, and metabolic acidosis. While primarily systemic, it presents critical ophthalmic risks including acute refractive shifts, snowflake cataracts, and the vision-threatening emergency of Rhino-orbital-cerebral Mucormycosis.

submissions.title: Diabetic Macular Edema (DME): The Master Clinician's Guide
submissions.summary: DME is the leading cause of vision loss in the working-age population. This comprehensive guide covers the intricate pathophysiology, evolving classification systems, and the evidence-based management protocols established by landmark clinical trials.

submissions.title: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion (BRVO): The Ultimate Clinical Guide
submissions.summary: BRVO is the second most common retinal vascular disease after diabetic retinopathy, typically occurring at arteriovenous crossings. This guide covers the pathophysiology, evidence-based management (Anti-VEGF/Laser), and landmark clinical trials like BRAVO and VIBRANT.

submissions.title: Pars Plana Vitrectomy (PPV) in Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy
submissions.summary: Master the surgical management of advanced PDR, focusing on the indications, biomechanical steps of fibrovascular membrane dissection, and the prevention of intraoperative catastrophe.

submissions.title: High-Risk Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (HR-PDR)
submissions.summary: High-Risk PDR represents a critical threshold in diabetic eye disease where the risk of severe vision loss (SVL) increases exponentially. This guide covers the landmark DRS criteria, multimodal imaging, and the evolving paradigm of PRP vs. Anti-VEGF therapy.

submissions.title: Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR): Mastery of Pathogenesis and Management
submissions.summary: PDR represents the advanced stage of diabetic eye disease, characterized by retinal ischemia leading to neovascularization. This infographic outlines the clinical trajectory from hypoxia to sight-threatening complications.

submissions.title: Diabetic Retinopathy: From NPDR to PDR
submissions.summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to the staging, progression, and evidence-based management of diabetic retinopathy, transition from non-proliferative to proliferative stages.

submissions.title: Mastering Panretinal Photocoagulation (PRP): The Gold Standard in Ischemic Retinopathy
submissions.summary: PRP remains the definitive treatment for proliferative diabetic retinopathy and other ischemic retinal diseases by inducing regression of neovascularization through the destruction of metabolically active peripheral retina. This infographic serves as a comprehensive clinical guide for the modern ophthalmologist.

submissions.title: Advanced Diabetic Eye Disease: Mastering TRD & End-Stage PDR
submissions.summary: Advanced Diabetic Eye Disease (ADED) represents the sight-threatening zenith of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, characterized by Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD), persistent vitreous hemorrhage, and fibrovascular proliferation. This guide provides a residency-level deep dive into its surgical and clinical management.

submissions.title: Mastering Tractional Retinal Detachment (TRD) & Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy
submissions.summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to the diagnosis, pathophysiology, and management of Tractional Retinal Detachment, specifically in the context of advanced Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR) with vitreous hemorrhage.

submissions.title: Retinal Masterclass: Vascular, Degenerative & Hereditary Disorders
submissions.summary: An exhaustive clinical guide to the diagnosis and management of retinal pathologies, ranging from Diabetic Retinopathy and Vascular Occlusions to complex Hereditary Dystrophies. This visual compendium integrates international study protocols with gold-standard diagnostic criteria.

submissions.title: Diabetic Eye Disease: Screening Guidelines & Management
submissions.summary: This visual guide outlines the UK National Screening Committee's systematic approach to testing for diabetic retinopathy. It covers the methods, classification systems, and specific referral timelines for clinical management and hospital eye services.

submissions.title: DIABETIC EYE DISEASE: A GLOBAL CLINICAL OVERVIEW
submissions.summary: An exhaustive guide to the classification, systemic impact, and ophthalmic complications of diabetes mellitus. This overview includes diagnostic criteria and critical findings from landmark clinical trials like DCCT, UKPDS, and ACCORD.

submissions.title: DIABETIC EYE DISEASE: SYSTEMIC MANAGEMENT
submissions.summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to the systemic management of diabetic eye disease. This resource covers glycaemic, blood pressure, and cholesterol control targets, lifestyle interventions, renal support, and pregnancy screening protocols.

submissions.title: VIP:::FRCS:EMERGENCY MEDICINE FOR FRCS: STROKE & ENDOCRINE CRISES
submissions.summary: A comprehensive clinical guide for the FRCS (Glasg) Exam covering Acute Stroke, Intracranial Pressure, Diabetic Emergencies (DKA, HONK, Hypoglycemia), and Thyroid/Adrenal crises. Designed for rapid review of diagnostic pointers and management protocols.

submissions.title: DIABETIC EYE DISEASE: ASSESSMENT & MANAGEMENT
submissions.summary: A comprehensive clinical framework for the assessment, grading, and treatment of diabetic eye disease. This guide integrates risk factor evaluation, the Airlie House/ETDRS classification systems, and specific management protocols for retinopathy and maculopathy.

submissions.title: PRP: Pan-Retinal Photocoagulation Mastery
submissions.summary: The definitive surgical laser intervention for ischemic retinal diseases, primarily Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy (PDR). By selectively destroying peripheral photoreceptors, PRP reduces metabolic demand and suppresses the production of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF).

submissions.title: Mastering Diabetic Macular Edema (DME)
submissions.summary: Diabetic Macular Edema (DME) is the leading cause of moderate vision loss in the working-age population. This poster provides a deep-dive into its pathophysiology, evidence-based management, and the latest landmark clinical trials.

submissions.title: Navigating the Cutting Edge: Today's Trends in Ophthalmic Research
submissions.summary: Dive into the dynamic world of ophthalmic literature! This poster illuminates the most vibrant and impactful research trends shaping modern ophthalmology, from groundbreaking AI applications to revolutionary gene therapies and advanced surgical innovations. Stay ahead of the curve and understand the drivers, implications, and future directions of ophthalmic science.

submissions.title: DCR Bleeding: Surgical Anatomy, Prevention & Hemostasis
submissions.summary: A definitive, textbook-grade clinical guide on managing intraoperative and postoperative epistaxis and orbital hemorrhage during Dacryocystorhinostomy (External and Endonasal DCR). Details vascular anatomy, risk mitigation, packing techniques, and step-by-step hemostatic algorithms.

submissions.title: DCR Bleeding: Surgical Anatomy, Prevention & Hemostasis
submissions.summary: A definitive, textbook-grade clinical guide on managing intraoperative and postoperative epistaxis and orbital hemorrhage during Dacryocystorhinostomy (External and Endonasal DCR). Details vascular anatomy, risk mitigation, packing techniques, and step-by-step hemostatic algorithms.

submissions.title: Unraveling IgG4-Related Ophthalmic Disease (IgG4-ROD): A Comprehensive Guide
submissions.summary: IgG4-Related Ophthalmic Disease (IgG4-ROD) is a fascinating and increasingly recognized systemic fibroinflammatory condition that frequently manifests in the orbit and ocular adnexa. This poster delves into the intricate details of IgG4-ROD, from its elusive pathophysiology to its multi-faceted clinical presentation, diagnostic challenges, and evolving management strategies, offering a deep dive for ophthalmology residents and fellows.

submissions.title: IgG4-Related Ophthalmic Disease (IgG4-ROD)
submissions.summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to IgG4-Related Ophthalmic Disease (IgG4-ROD), a fibroinflammatory systemic condition that commonly masquerades as idiopathic orbital inflammation, thyroid eye disease, or lymphoma. This poster outlines the pathophysiology, diagnostic criteria, histopathological hallmarks, and evidence-based management protocols essential for ophthalmologists.

submissions.title: Optic Pathway Glioma: Clinical Masterclass
submissions.summary: Optic Pathway Gliomas (OPGs) are low-grade astrocytic tumors affecting the optic nerve, chiasm, and post-chiasmatic tracts, predominantly occurring in young children. Strongly associated with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1), management balances preservation of visual function, endocrine stability, and tumor control through multi-disciplinary care.

submissions.title: Optic Pathway Glioma: Clinical Masterclass
submissions.summary: Optic Pathway Gliomas (OPGs) are low-grade astrocytic tumors affecting the optic nerve, chiasm, and post-chiasmatic tracts, predominantly occurring in young children. Strongly associated with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1), management balances preservation of visual function, endocrine stability, and tumor control through multi-disciplinary care.

submissions.title: Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking (CXL): The 'Sub-400nm' Revolution for Ectasia Management
submissions.summary: Corneal Collagen Cross-linking (CXL) is a transformative, minimally invasive ophthalmic procedure utilizing ultraviolet A (UVA) light (specifically in the 'sub-400nm' range, typically 365-370nm) and a photosensitizer, riboflavin, to biomechanically stiffen the corneal stroma. This process effectively halts the progression of ectatic corneal diseases like keratoconus and post-LASIK ectasia, preserving vision and preventing the need for corneal transplantation.

submissions.title: Sub-400 µm Corneal Cross-Linking (CXL): Advanced Protocols for Thin Corneas
submissions.summary: A comprehensive clinical reference on managing progressive corneal ectasia in corneas thinner than 400 µm. Details photonics, modified protocols (hypo-osmolar, CACXL, SLACXL, sub-400 individualized fluence), endothelial safety thresholds, and high-yield surgical pearls.

approved.title: Clinical Mastery: Ocular Manifestations of Histiocytosis
approved.summary: Histiocytosis encompasses a group of rare, heterogeneous disorders characterized by the abnormal proliferation and accumulation of histiocytes (macrophages/dendritic cells). In ophthalmology, these systemic diseases frequently present with orbital involvement, proptosis, and eyelid lesions.
